name: Google Summer of Code
description: Paid open source contribution programme. Contributors work with a mentoring organisation on a project over the summer, with a stipend paid on completion.
notes: Worldwide, no location restriction. Contributor applications open in March and close late March; the 2027 date has not been announced, so no deadline is stored. Start talking to mentoring organisations in February.

name: Outreachy
description: Paid, fully remote internships in open source and open science for people who face underrepresentation or systemic bias in tech where they live. $7,000 USD stipend, three months.
notes: Two cohorts a year. The December 2026 cohort closed on 31 August 2026. The next intake is the May 2027 cohort, with applications expected in early February 2027. Open to applicants from any country.

name: MLH Fellowship
description: A remote internship alternative where fellows contribute to real open source projects in small pods with mentorship. Runs in batches through the year.
notes: Batch-based rather than a single annual deadline. Confirm country eligibility and stipend terms on the current programme page before applying.

name: ALX Africa
description: Pan-African tech training and career acceleration programmes, including software engineering, data and cloud tracks. Free to participants, remote-first, aimed at early-career Africans.
notes: Africa-focused, rolling intakes rather than fixed deadlines. Also hires directly: their own board is on Greenhouse and is collected by the ATS adapter.

name: Andela
description: Global talent marketplace that began as an African developer training and placement company. Places engineers with international clients.
notes: No longer runs the original multi-year training fellowship; now a talent marketplace. Worth watching for placements that accept Ethiopia specifically.

name: MEST Africa
description: Pan-African training programme and incubator for software entrepreneurs, with a year-long fellowship covering engineering, business and product.
notes: Annual intake, usually opening mid-year, with travel expected for parts of the programme. Verify whether Ethiopia is a covered country for the current cohort.

name: Zindi
description: Competition platform for African data scientists and machine learning engineers. Prizes, hiring pipelines, and a portfolio you can show publicly.
notes: Continuous competitions with per-competition deadlines rather than one programme date. Useful as a proof-of-skill route when you have no industry experience yet.

name: Deep Learning Indaba
description: Annual African machine learning gathering with workshops, tutorials and travel bursaries for students across the continent.
notes: Annual, usually around August/September, with a bursary application window several months earlier. Moving target: check the current year's page.
